prompt.brief: Design a compliance and audit platform that immutably captures cloud API activity and configuration changes, evaluates controls, detects threats, and produces evidence for PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2.
successSignals: Make append-only, time-synchronized audit events the evidence source and derive searchable findings, controls, and dashboards.
Prevent tampering with encryption, retention locks, chained integrity proofs, restricted access, and independent account storage.
Evaluate configuration continuously, correlate activity with identity and asset context, and route high-severity violations quickly.
Explain missing events, duplicate delivery, legal holds, tenant isolation, privacy, retention, evidence export, and replay.

functional: Collect API logs, identity activity, configuration snapshots, vulnerability findings, and policy evaluations from cloud accounts.
Search events and findings, show asset history and control status, assign remediation, and export signed audit evidence.
Support control versions, exceptions with expiry, incident escalation, legal holds, retention rules, and auditor access.
nonFunctional: Retain required audit evidence for seven years with searchable recent data and lower-cost immutable archive tiers.
Ingest bursty multi-account activity without dropping events or allowing one account to monopolize processing.
Make collection, policy evaluation, notifications, and remediation idempotent with explicit event completeness tracking.
Continue collecting and preserving evidence during rule-engine, search, dashboard, or notification outages.
scaleAssumptions: Monitor 10,000 cloud accounts, 100 million events per day, and seven years of retained evidence.
Partition by tenant, account, event day, and asset; isolate high-volume accounts and bursty control-plane services.
Keep recent indexes bounded while preserving encrypted raw events, snapshots, findings, and integrity proofs in archive.

dataFlow.description: The audit service durably records normalized activity, actor/resource identity, policy context, and an integrity chain.

dataFlow.title: Serve and recover asynchronously

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Compliance commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Compliance writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Compliance version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Compliance by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Compliance work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Compliance projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Compliance projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Compliance records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Compliance latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines evidence capture, control evaluation, auditability, scale, retention, and failure contracts.
Entities and actor/resource/time keys support audit search, controls, evidence integrity, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Compliance consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
